data.prompt: Instrumental only, no vocals. Create a 120-second original game background track at exactly 96 BPM in 4/4, centered on D Dorian. Design this as a continuous loop-friendly cosmic pinball soundtrack, atmospheric and quietly propulsive rather than combat music. A midnight-blue observatory among swirling galaxies: warm analog pads, slowly evolving airy granular textures, a restrained rounded sub-bass, luminous glass-marimba notes, sparse celesta-like star sparkles, delicate filtered eighth-note arpeggios, soft kick and brushed electronic percussion, and occasional tiny dry mechanical tick accents suggesting precision brass clockwork. Wonder, elegant motion, concentration, hopeful mystery. Moderate-low arrangement density, warm low mids and silky airy highs; leave ample transient space for pinball impacts, no huge snare, no harsh distortion, no piercing lead, no aggressive bass drop, no cinematic explosions, no voice or choir. Wide atmospheric pads with clear central pulse, clean professional production, stable loudness and gentle dynamics, no sudden changes. [0:00-0:20] Establish the ongoing soft groove immediately, without a fade-in or dramatic intro; pads, round bass, restrained mechanical ticks and a repeating delicate four-note celestial motif. Intensity 3/10. [0:20-1:00] Maintain the same tempo and harmonic loop; add a quiet sparkling arpeggio and subtle syncopated mallet answers, slowly drifting stereo atmosphere. Intensity 4/10. [1:00-1:40] Broaden the glowing pads and introduce restrained higher octave bell responses, modest lift suggesting a nebula opening; retain soft groove and uncluttered mix. Intensity 5/10. [1:40-2:00] Return gradually to the opening instrumentation, harmony and four-note motif, keep rhythm continuous to the final bar, finish in a state compatible with the opening rather than a cadence. No fade-out, no ending flourish, no silence at either boundary. Build a musically continuous loop at the start/end boundary. Instrumental only, no vocals.
